metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Wyalusing, PA | Bradford County
metaDescription: Wyalusing, Bradford County mineral owner? You're in the most active dry gas county in PA. We buy directly, with a real lease review first.
heroLead: Wyalusing sits along the Susquehanna River in Bradford County, which has more producing Marcellus wells than any other county in Pennsylvania.
intro: If you had to pick the single county that put Pennsylvania dry gas on the map, it would be Bradford County, and Wyalusing sits right inside that story. Chesapeake Energy leased and drilled here aggressively in the earliest years of the boom, and Bradford County has held its position as the most heavily drilled county in the state ever since.
That much history means Wyalusing-area interests come with a lot of production data behind them, which we treat as an advantage in putting together an accurate offer.

sections.heading: The Most Drilled County in Pennsylvania
paragraphs: Bradford County has consistently led the state in producing Marcellus well count, with Chesapeake Energy as the dominant historical operator and Coterra Energy now managing much of that legacy acreage following its merger. Wyalusing sits in a part of the county that saw some of the earliest and most concentrated development.
That intensity means most Wyalusing-area units have years, sometimes over a decade, of production history we can review directly, rather than relying on projections.

sections.heading: Chesapeake's Legacy Leases
paragraphs: A lot of the leases signed in Bradford County during the earliest boom years came from Chesapeake's aggressive early leasing campaigns, some of which carried terms that later drew scrutiny and litigation statewide over post-production deduction practices. If your Wyalusing-area lease traces back to that era, understanding exactly what deduction language it contains is especially important.
We review those older Chesapeake-originated leases carefully, since their specific wording has real consequences for what you've actually been receiving versus what the lease technically allows.

sections.heading: River Town, Long Family Histories
paragraphs: Wyalusing's location along the Susquehanna made it prime farmland long before it became prime gas ground, and a lot of the mineral interests here trace back through several generations of the same families. We approach every one of those interests knowing there's likely real history behind the parcel, well beyond a line on a spreadsheet.

faqs.question: Is Bradford County really the most drilled county in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: Yes, it has consistently ranked as having the highest number of producing Marcellus wells of any Pennsylvania county, with Chesapeake Energy and now Coterra as the leading historical operators.

faqs.question: My lease was originally signed with Chesapeake. Does that matter now?
faqs.answer: It can. Some early Chesapeake leases carried deduction language that later drew legal scrutiny. We review the specific wording of your lease to understand what it actually allows.

faqs.question: How much production history is typically available for a Wyalusing-area unit?
faqs.answer: Many units here have been producing for over a decade, giving us substantial data to evaluate trends and estimate remaining value accurately.

faqs.question: Do you handle interests that changed operator hands through a merger?
faqs.answer: Yes. We regularly work with interests where the original leasing company, like Chesapeake, has since merged or sold its position to another operator, such as Coterra.
